risks.description: Full literal value-by-value re-audit of the homepage at TRUE desktop width (1440px) -- prior verification rounds were done against the browser panes default scaled-down width (580-800px), where vw-based clamp() typography sits near its minimum and would look deceptively close even when the max-width value was wrong. Re-testing at 1440px surfaced real, previously-undetected mismatches: (1) SYSTEMIC button shape -- .hero-cta/.btn was border-radius:999px (full pill) with padding 11px/18px across the ENTIRE site (every CTA button, all sections), when the literal mockup value is border-radius:5px, padding:16px/24px -- a fully rounded pill vs a barely-rounded rectangle is a highly visible shape difference; (2) hero h1 clamp max was 96px (comment said measured from a screenshot) vs literal 112px, plus wrong line-height (1.05 vs .88) and missing letter-spacing; (3) pod card image aspect-ratio was 1:1 (square) vs literal 4:5 (portrait), plus name/description/price/badge type sizes were all off by several px each (reusing generic collection-card-* sizes instead of the pod-system-specific literal values); (4) pod bundle bar was a generic small-text navy bar instead of the literal larger-scale treatment (24px price -> 36px, 8px radius -> 14px, symmetric padding -> asymmetric, price+compare stacked wrong).
risks.mitigation: All items above fixed and reverified via getComputedStyle at 1440px viewport (not screenshot-only, since the browser panes visibility toggled unpredictably mid-session -- computed-style checks do not depend on the pane being visible/foregrounded). Remaining confirmed-correct-already: section backgrounds, section padding rhythm, section heading clamp sizes, trust crests, subscribe bullets/price/frequency, testimonials cards, faq typography, newsletter stat sizes -- all independently re-verified this round, not just carried over from memory.

Add to bag / Add all 5 buttons: since wiring them to a real product would require inventing a fake product mapping (dishonest -- a customer clicking Car Soap would add a random snowboard to their real cart), left as disabled buttons with a clear title explaining why, ready to activate automatically once real Car Brite SKUs exist in the store. details.trigger: User shared a screenshot (their own local dev server, not this sessions) showing the Tire & Wheels pod cards button area looking cut/misaligned compared to its neighbors.
details.root_cause: The Buy X on Amazon link text length varies by product name (Buy Car Soap on Amazon vs Buy Interior Cleaner on Amazon) with no white-space/overflow handling -- on a narrower viewport than was tested earlier this session, a longer label could wrap to a second line while shorter ones stayed on one, pushing that one card taller/misaligned relative to its row neighbors.
details.fix: Wrapped the amazon-link text in a span and added overflow:hidden;white-space:nowrap;text-overflow:ellipsis (plus min-width:0, the common flexbox truncation gotcha) so every card in the row stays exactly the same height regardless of product-name length or viewport width -- verified at a deliberately narrow 1024px width where the bug would be most likely: all 5 cards now measure an identical 43px amazon-button height, longer labels truncate with an ellipsis instead of wrapping.
details.scope: Applied to both the homepage pod cards (_index.jsx) and the Collection page product cards (CollectionProductCard.jsx) for consistency, even though the latters fixed Buy on Amazon text was lower-risk.
